answers.primary: A subagent owns this: either the built-in general-purpose agent asked ad hoc ("use a subagent to run the test suite and report only the failing tests with their error messages") or, if it recurs, a custom .claude/agents/test-runner.md with tools Bash, Read, Grep, Glob and a body that specifies the exact report shape. The suite runs inside the subagent's own context window and only its final report is appended to the main conversation.
answers.rejected_alternative: A skill holding the same instructions. Rejected because a skill's steps execute in the invoking conversation, so every line of log output lands in the very context window the user is trying to protect.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, with the harness owning the boundary and the model owning the content. The harness guarantees that the raw stdout physically cannot enter the parent context; nothing guarantees the subagent's summary is faithful, so which failures get reported is a model judgment.
answers.context_boundary: Two windows. Inbound to the subagent: Claude's delegation message, the agent's own system prompt, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and a git status snapshot. Outbound to the main conversation: one final text report, scanned by the harness for instruction-shaped patterns before Claude reads it.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when Claude delegates, by description match, natural-language request, or @-mention. It ends when the subagent emits its report; the instance can be revived later with SendMessage, and its transcript persists under ~/.claude/projects/.../subagents/ for cleanupPeriodDays (30 by default).
answers.failure_mode: Fails open on fidelity. A subagent that drops or paraphrases a failure produces a clean-looking summary with no signal that anything was lost, and a subagent that dumps the whole log back defeats the purpose entirely. Recovery means re-running or opening the subagent transcript file, since the raw output never existed in the main context.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.198 subagents run in the background by default, which narrows their built-in tool pool (Bash, Read, Grep, Glob survive, so test running is fine) and surfaces permission prompts in the main session. v2.1.211 makes background results arrive as a completion notification in a later turn. Output scanning of the final report requires v2.1.210 or later. Spawns count against the 200-per-session cap (v2.1.212+) and the 20-concurrent cap (v2.1.217+).

answers.primary: A custom subagent at .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md whose frontmatter carries a tools allowlist of exactly Read, Grep, Glob. The allowlist is resolved when the subagent is spawned, so the model is never handed Edit, Write, NotebookEdit or Bash and cannot call what it does not have, regardless of what its prompt or its mid-task reasoning says.
answers.rejected_alternative: disallowedTools: Write, Edit on the same definition. Rejected because it only subtracts from an otherwise inherited pool and leaves Bash in place, and Bash can modify the repository freely with a redirect, sed, or git checkout.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Tool availability is decided by the permission and agent-loading layer before the model's first turn, which is what makes this structural rather than instructional.
answers.context_boundary: The subagent gets a fresh isolated context: its markdown body as system prompt, Claude's delegation message, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and a git status snapshot. Only its final review report crosses back; its file reads and greps never enter the main window.
answers.lifecycle: Applies on every spawn of that agent type and lasts for that invocation. The definition file is watched, so edits take effect on the next delegation within seconds without a restart, unless the .claude/agents/ directory did not exist when the session started.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed, which is the point, but the closure can be silently relocated. A same-named definition at a higher-priority scope (managed settings, then --agents, then project, then user, then plugin) shadows yours, and two files declaring the same name inside one directory resolve by filesystem read order with no documented precedence. Note also that this constrains only the worker: the main session retains full write access.
answers.version_caveat: From v2.1.208, a tools list where nothing resolves refuses to launch with an error naming the bad entries; before that the subagent launched tool-less and returned empty or confusing results. Background subagents (the default since v2.1.198) get a further-narrowed built-in set, though Read, Grep and Glob all survive it. If the parent session runs bypassPermissions or acceptEdits, that permission mode takes precedence over the subagent's, but it does not restore tools the allowlist omitted.

answers.primary: The built-in /btw side-question command, not a custom extension mechanism at all. It answers from the full current conversation, has no tool access, and renders the exchange in a dismissible overlay that never enters the transcript.
answers.rejected_alternative: A subagent. The docs frame /btw as its exact inverse: a subagent has full tools but starts from an empty context, so it would have to rediscover everything already discussed and its result would then be appended to history.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Toollessness and the exclusion from conversation history are properties of the command, not behaviours the model is asked to observe.
answers.context_boundary: It runs against the live parent conversation and reuses that conversation's prompt cache, so cost is minimal. Nothing crosses back into the session: the answer exists only in the overlay, and earlier side questions stay listed there until cleared with x.
answers.lifecycle: Fires on /btw <question>, including while Claude is mid-turn on something else, and produces exactly one response with no follow-ups. It stops applying the moment the overlay is dismissed with Space, Enter or Escape; pressing f forks it into a new session where the question and answer become real transcript turns with tool access.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and low-stakes, but it fails silently on staleness. Because it cannot read files, run commands or search, it will answer confidently from whatever version of the code entered context earlier in the session, even if the file has since changed. Being single-shot, an ambiguous question cannot be clarified in place.
answers.version_caveat: Bare /btw with no question reopens the most recent overlay only from v2.1.212; earlier versions printed a usage message. Stepping between earlier answers with Left and Right requires v2.1.187 or later. The f fork action is available in local sessions only.

answers.primary: A forked subagent started with /subtask, for example "/subtask draft regression tests for the connection-reset bug we just characterized". A fork inherits the entire conversation so far plus the main session's system prompt, tools and model, so every finding, ruled-out hypothesis, config quirk and stack trace is already in front of it with nothing re-explained.
answers.rejected_alternative: A named subagent such as a test-writer definition. Rejected because a non-fork subagent starts from a fresh context and receives only the delegation message Claude composes, which means two hours of accumulated debugging state would have to be summarised by hand or lost.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model owns the outcome, since a fork is a full agent with the parent's tool pool and permission context. The harness owns only the mechanics: copying the conversation in, and keeping the fork's own tool calls out of the main window.
answers.context_boundary: The fork gets a snapshot copy of the parent conversation at the instant it spawns and shares the parent's prompt cache, which makes it cheaper than a fresh subagent. Only its final result crosses back as a message; its intermediate reads and test runs stay in its own window, and nothing said in the main session after the spawn reaches it unless explicitly sent.
answers.lifecycle: Starts on /subtask and runs in the background in a panel below the prompt while the user keeps working on the fix. It ends when it returns its result or when the user presses x on its row; it spends the same per-session subagent budget as an ordinary subagent, and a fork cannot spawn further forks.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open. The fork carries the parent's full write tools and permission context, so it can edit the same files being worked on concurrently and produce conflicting changes, and a backgrounded fork's edits fall outside the session's checkpoints so /rewind will not undo them (git is the only recovery). The inherited context is frozen at spawn time, so conclusions reached afterwards silently do not reach it.
answers.version_caveat: /subtask requires v2.1.212 or later; on v2.1.161 through v2.1.211 the command was /fork, and on v2.1.117 through v2.1.160 it needed CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1. Letting Claude itself spawn forks is explicitly experimental and subject to a staged rollout. When agent view is turned off, /subtask is unavailable and /fork starts the forked subagent instead of copying the session.

answers.primary: A skill at .claude/skills/pr-summary/SKILL.md carrying the written procedure, with frontmatter context: fork, agent: Explore, and disable-model-invocation: true so it runs only when a person types /pr-summary. The SKILL.md body becomes the forked subagent's prompt, and Explore supplies a read-only tool set with Write and Edit denied; add allowed-tools: Bash(gh *) if the procedure shells out to the GitHub CLI.
answers.rejected_alternative: A custom read-only subagent in .claude/agents/ invoked by @-mention. Rejected because it puts the procedure in a system prompt and leaves the actual task to whatever delegation message Claude improvises, whereas the team wants the written procedure itself to be the prompt and to register as a named slash command.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness owns both hard requirements: the fork's context isolation keeps intermediate output out of the invoking conversation, and the Explore agent type denies Write and Edit. The model owns only whether it actually follows the steps in the procedure.
answers.context_boundary: The fully rendered SKILL.md, with any inline shell substitutions already expanded before Claude sees anything, is the forked subagent's entire prompt. With agent: Explore it does not receive the invoking conversation, CLAUDE.md, or the git status snapshot; only the final summary returns.
answers.lifecycle: Triggered by /pr-summary. It runs in the background by default and the result arrives in the conversation when it completes; set background: false to block the invoking turn instead. It stops applying when the fork finishes, and disable-model-invocation keeps Claude from starting it on its own.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on writes and on context leakage, but has two quiet traps. A backgrounded fork runs with the narrower background tool set, so a step needing a tool outside it just does not work and the report comes back thin; and because Explore skips CLAUDE.md, project rules the procedure implicitly depends on never reach it. A context: fork skill that is guidelines rather than an actionable task returns nothing useful.
answers.version_caveat: background: false requires v2.1.218 or later; before that a forked skill always blocked the invoking turn. The ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} substitution inside allowed-tools needs v2.1.129 or later. Inline shell substitution can be switched off organization-wide with disableSkillShellExecution, and a project skill's allowed-tools only take effect after the workspace trust dialog is accepted for that folder.

answers.primary: The skills frontmatter field on the worker's own definition: .claude/agents/api-developer.md with skills: [api-conventions]. That field injects the full body of the named skill into the subagent's context at startup, not merely its description, so every run begins with the conventions text present.
answers.rejected_alternative: Leaving the conventions as an ordinary skill and relying on the Skill tool. Rejected because that puts only the description in context and makes loading a model decision, which is exactly the discoverable-but-ignored behaviour being complained about.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split. The harness guarantees the text is present at turn zero; the model still owns whether it complies with it, so this buys guaranteed availability, not guaranteed adherence.
answers.context_boundary: The subagent's own fresh window. Inbound: the agent's markdown body as system prompt, the full preloaded skill content, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, a git status snapshot, and Claude's delegation message. Outbound: only the subagent's report. The main session's copy of the guidance is irrelevant, since conversation history never crosses into a non-fork subagent.
answers.lifecycle: Applies at every spawn of that agent type and ends when the subagent returns. It does not apply when the same definition is used as an agent teams teammate, because teammates load skills from project and user settings instead and ignore the definition's skills field.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory once loaded, and silently degrading when misconfigured. If the named skill is missing, renamed, or disabled, Claude Code skips it and logs only a debug-log warning, so the worker launches with no conventions and the failure looks identical to the original complaint. For real enforcement, pair it with a PostToolUse hook or a reviewer pass.
answers.version_caveat: A skill with disable-model-invocation: true cannot be preloaded, because preloading draws from the same pool Claude may invoke; from v2.1.215 that also excludes the bundled /verify and /code-review skills. Listing Skill in the tools field is not how you preload, and omitting Skill from tools blocks runtime skill invocation without affecting this field.

answers.primary: A custom subagent with tools: Bash plus a PreToolUse hook declared in its own frontmatter, matcher "Bash", running a validation script that reads the tool input JSON from stdin, inspects tool_input.command, and exits with code 2 on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE or CREATE. Exit code 2 blocks the call before execution and feeds the stderr text back to the worker as the refusal reason.
answers.rejected_alternative: permissions.deny Bash rules. Rejected because deny rules cannot carry allowlist exceptions (a broad deny beats a narrower allow), and Claude Code explicitly refuses to match a tool's primary content field, so a rule like Bash(command:UPDATE *) is ignored with a startup warning as trivially bypassable by a compound command.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. The hook is an external process invoked by Claude Code before the tool runs, and its exit code decides the call, so the worker's own reasoning is not in the loop.
answers.context_boundary: The hook runs outside every model context, as an OS process in the main session, receiving JSON on stdin that includes the command plus agent_id and agent_type identifying which subagent asked. Nothing of the worker's context crosses out; only the stderr block reason crosses back into the worker's window.
answers.lifecycle: Fires before every Bash call while that subagent is active and is torn down when the subagent finishes. Declaring the same hook in settings.json instead would make it session-wide and cover the main conversation too.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed when it runs, but fails open when it does not. A script that is missing, not marked executable on macOS or Linux, or skipped because the project folder was never trusted, means the hook errors and the mutation proceeds. Pattern matching is also evadable in ways that matter here: a mutating statement inside a file passed with sqlcmd -i, a here-doc, or a stored procedure call never matches the word-boundary regex, so a read-only database credential remains the only genuinely deterministic control.
answers.version_caveat: From v2.1.218 a project-level subagent's frontmatter hooks run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted for the folder containing the agent file; until then the subagent still runs but its hooks are silently skipped with a debug-log error. Plugin-supplied subagents ignore the hooks field entirely for security reasons. On Windows the validator must be PowerShell with shell: powershell on the hook entry, and hook allow decisions never override a matching deny or ask permission rule.

answers.primary: A skill at .claude/skills/cleanup/SKILL.md with disallowed-tools: AskUserQuestion and disable-model-invocation: true. The first removes AskUserQuestion from Claude's available tool pool while the skill is active, and the second makes /cleanup the only way to start it. This is the documented use for the field: an autonomous loop that must never call a particular tool.
answers.rejected_alternative: A permissions.deny rule for AskUserQuestion in settings.json. Rejected because a deny rule is session-wide and permanent, so it would also gag Claude during ordinary interactive work and would not restore the capability by itself when the user speaks again.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. The tool is removed from the pool the model is offered, so refusing to ask is not a behaviour the routine has to remember.
answers.context_boundary: The main conversation, since a skill without context: fork runs in-session. The rendered SKILL.md enters the conversation as one message and stays for the rest of the session, while the tool-pool restriction lives in harness-side turn state rather than as text the model could argue with.
answers.lifecycle: Takes effect the moment /cleanup is invoked and clears when the user sends their next message, which is exactly the requested restore semantics and needs no cleanup step. Note the asymmetry: the instructions persist for the session, the restriction does not.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on the question tool, but the scoping is the trap. Because the grant clears at the next user message, a genuinely long routine that spans several user turns loses its protection after the first one, and Claude can prompt again on later turns. If the routine must never ask across its whole life, run it as a subagent instead, where AskUserQuestion is stripped unconditionally. The field also cannot remove EndConversation while other tools remain.
answers.version_caveat: disallowed-tools is a Claude Code extension to the Agent Skills open standard, so it does not carry to other tools that read the same SKILL.md. Project skill frontmatter takes effect only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted for the repository. From v2.1.196 disable-model-invocation also prevents the skill from running when a scheduled task fires with it as the prompt, and it blocks preloading the skill into subagents.

answers.primary: An agent team: the main session becomes the lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session with its own context window, coordinating through the shared task list and messaging each other by name with SendMessage. This is the documented competing-hypotheses pattern, phrased to the lead as "spawn 5 teammates to investigate different hypotheses, have them talk to each other to try to disprove each other's theories".
answers.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents. Rejected on the one requirement that decides it: subagents report only to the agent that spawned them and cannot talk to each other, so the adversarial cross-examination that makes the surviving theory trustworthy is impossible.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model, throughout. The lead decides team size, task decomposition, assignment and when the investigation is finished; the harness supplies only the plumbing, namely the per-agent mailbox JSON files, the shared task directory, and file locking so two teammates cannot claim the same task.
answers.context_boundary: Five separate context windows plus the lead's. Each teammate loads project context like a regular session (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) but does not inherit the lead's conversation history. What crosses between them: the spawn prompt, SendMessage mailbox messages delivered automatically, shared task-list state, plan-approval requests, and idle notifications.
answers.lifecycle: The team forms when the lead spawns the first teammate and lives for the session. Teammates run until they go idle, are asked by name to shut down (which they may approve or reject), or the session ends; the team config directory is deleted at session end while the task list persists under cleanupPeriodDays. TeammateIdle, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted hooks can gate the transitions.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open in several documented ways. Task status lags because teammates forget to mark work complete, which blocks dependent tasks; the lead frequently declares the investigation finished before it is, or starts doing the work itself instead of waiting; teammates stop on errors rather than recovering; and /resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates, after which the lead messages agents that no longer exist. Token cost scales linearly with five independent sessions.
answers.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default: requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, without which no team is created and Claude will not spawn teammates. Documented behaviour is v2.1.178 and later, where TeamCreate and TeamDelete no longer exist and the team_name field is deprecated. Structural limits: one team per session, no nested teams, the lead cannot be transferred, and permission modes are fixed at spawn. Split panes need tmux or iTerm2 with the it2 CLI and are unsupported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal and Ghostty.

answers.primary: Move the rule out of CLAUDE.md and into harness-enforced deny rules in .claude/settings.json: permissions.deny with Read(vendor/**) and Edit(vendor/**). The cause of the symptom is specific: Explore and Plan are the only subagents that skip the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, and delegated research is exactly what goes to them, with no frontmatter field or per-agent setting to change that. Deny rules are evaluated before ask and allow and are checked at every tool call regardless of which context window issued it.
answers.rejected_alternative: Defining a project subagent named Explore in .claude/agents/, which overrides the built-in and, being a custom agent, does load CLAUDE.md. Rejected because it merely restores the rule as text the model may or may not honour, and the requirement is that the searches stop happening, not that the searcher be told again.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. The permission layer denies the call; the rule text never reaches any model context, so there is nothing for a delegated agent to reason its way around.
answers.context_boundary: None, in the sense that the rule crosses no context boundary at all. It is loaded from settings at session start and applied by the permission layer to tool calls from the main conversation, subagents, forks, workflow agents and teammates alike, since teammates start with the lead's permission settings. All that reaches the agent is a denial.
answers.lifecycle: Active from session start for the whole session, and for every agent spawned within it, until the setting is removed. Deny beats every other scope: a managed-settings deny cannot be overridden by --allowedTools, and a user-level deny blocks a project-level allow.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for Read and Edit, but partially open for search, which is the half the user cares about. Claude Code only makes a best-effort attempt to extend Read rules to Grep and Glob, and Read and Edit rules do not cover arbitrary subprocesses, so a Python script or an unrecognised shell search can still walk vendor/. For enforcement that binds every process, enable the sandbox, whose filesystem boundary merges sandbox.filesystem settings with the Read and Edit deny rules.
answers.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path only from v2.1.208; Write and NotebookEdit are never covered, and a Write(vendor/**) rule prints a startup warning telling you to use Edit(vendor/**) instead. Path anchoring differs by scope: in user settings a leading-slash path resolves under ~/.claude, so use // or ~/ for a rule meant to apply inside every project. Organizations can pin this with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly in managed settings.
